solution: After failing an exam and fearing her father's punishment, a daughter secretly altered her grade. Upon seeing that the score had been changed using a green pen, the father realized his daughter was red-green colorblind. However, as he possessed normal vision and did not carry the relevant gene, it was impossible for his daughter to be colorblind. Realizing she was not his biological child, he flew into a rage and, in a fit of impulse, killed both his wife and daughter.
canonical_facts: The daughter alters a failed examination grade because she fears punishment
She uses green ink without recognizing the color
The father interprets this as red-green colorblindness
Believing his normal vision rules out this inheritance, he concludes she is not biologically his
He kills his wife and daughter in anger; describe his inference as the story’s belief, not a scientifically established paternity test
